claims.claim: Origen of Alexandria was a Christian theologian and biblical scholar who taught at the Catechetical School of Alexandria and later founded a school in Caesarea; he lived circa 185–254 CE, being born in Alexandria and dying in Tyre.
The Commentary on the Epistle to the Romans was composed around AD 246 while Origen was in Caesarea.
Origen wrote the work as an exegetical study of Paul’s letter to the Romans, intended for readers seeking a theological interpretation of that epistle.
The commentary was motivated by a need to counter Gnostic readings of Paul and to refute the “doctrine of natures,” which taught that human destiny is fixed at birth.
In doing so Origen defended the Christian doctrine of free will against deterministic interpretations of predestination.

Only fragments of the original Greek archetype survive; the most complete transmission is through Rufinus’s Latin translation made circa 406 and through later Greek catena manuscripts such as Vatican Greek 762.
The commentary is the oldest extant continuous commentary on Romans and therefore provides a unique early patristic perspective on predestination, free will, and anti‑Gnostic theology.
